newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-WOODFORDE ESCAPES INTO SECOND ROUND AT NEWPORT.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WOODFORDE ESCAPES INTO SECOND ROUND AT NEWPORT.

text.p: Just two days after his historic Wimbledon doubles victory, Australian Mark Woodforde was pushed to the limit before advancing to the second round at the Hall of Fame Championships on Tuesday.

Second seed Woodforde, who teamed with countryman Todd Woodbridge to claim a fifth consecutive Wimbledon doubles title, had to win a second-set tie-break 7-4 to stay alive before pulling out a 4-6 7-6 7-5 win over American Steve Bryan.
Woodforde reached the fourth round in singles at Wimbledon before falling to Michael Stich, while his doubles partner was an unexpected semifinalist in singles.
Top seed Alex Radulescu of Germany also needed three sets to win his opening match in America's only grass court tournament on the ATP calendar.
Radulescu, who reached the third round at Wimbledon, held off American Vince Spadea 6-4 6-7 6-3.
Last year's runner-up Grant Stafford of South Africa, the third seed, ousted American Jeff Salzenstein 7-5 6-3.
But Nicolas Pereira of Venezuela is not defending his title, opting instead to represent his country in Davis Cup qualifying this weekend.

The tournament, with its usual weak field coming on the heels of Wimbledon when most of the world's top players take a breather before starting the summer hardcourt season, lost one seeded player Tuesday.
Little-known Marzio Martelli of Italy, the sixth seed, was bounced by American David Wheaton 4-6 6-4 6-2.
